justification: B sets the body in a larger, more legible Arabic face with numbered bold headings and consistent running headers, giving clearer structure. A's text is smaller and lightly set. Its first page breaks early, leaving a large empty gap. Its section rules and gray subheads are weaker. Both end with a sparse final page.

A sets Arabic in a larger, more open face with generous leading, and its headings are numbered (1, 2, 3.1) and distinctly bolder, so the structure reads clearly in both the table of contents and the body. B's text is smaller and denser, and its unnumbered headings are weak and barely distinct from body text, as with بسكرة and فاس on B5. The cover pages are comparable.

B adds a table of contents, numbered section headings and running headers, and keeps a consistent, generous body size, which gives clearer navigation and a steadier rhythm. A switches body size between the larger lead paragraphs and the smaller paragraphs that follow, which reads unevenly. A's mixed serif and Arabic setting has some appeal, but B's text pages are more uniform and easier to read. Both show broken image-markdown residue, and B's last page is mostly empty.

A sets the Arabic text in a Naskh-style face with comfortable leading, so long paragraphs read more easily. Its green section band gives the التسمية heading a clear structure (A3). B's sans Arabic is denser and tighter, and its section headings are plain numbered text. B does fill page 4 better, but A's page 5 leaves a large empty area. Both use the same image page.

B adds a table of contents on B2 and numbered section headings on B4–B5, which make the document easier to navigate. Its body text is also comfortably set. A's solid navy header bands on A2–A5 look heavier but polished. Overall B's added structure and clearer headings make it the better reading copy.

Design B pairs its body text with headers and footers on every page and a more cohesive column. Its headings are clearer, and the section heading sits flush with the text. In A, the first-page section heading overhangs the right margin, and the sub-label is styled in grey, which weakens the hierarchy. B's text is slightly larger, with comfortable leading. A's tighter sizing reads less easily, though it is compact.

A sets the Arabic in a Naskh-style face that reads comfortably in body text and has a clear running header with section names. B's geometric Kufi-style face is wider and less readable for long passages. B's heavy top rule on the inner pages and its "main article" line, which nearly matches the heading size, also weaken the hierarchy. Both designs paginate similarly.

A has a table of contents, numbered section headings with clear weight, running headers and rules, and more generous leading. B has no TOC, small unnumbered headings that barely stand out from the body, denser text, and a nearly empty final page.

B adds a table of contents, uses a consistent top rule and running header, and sets justified Arabic text with clear section headings. A's sections each start on a new page, which leaves pages part-empty, and A has no contents page. B's diacritic-heavy font is slightly busier, but its overall structure is stronger.

A keeps the image with its introducing text on A5, so the figure sits where it is announced. B pushes the image onto its own page B6, leaving B5 half empty and B6 mostly blank. That breaks the flow. B's green section band and running headers are a nice touch. Even so, A's pagination is tighter and more balanced.

A sets its section headings in bold with numbers (1, 2, 3), which gives a clearer hierarchy. B uses light, unnumbered headings with rules above them, and these read weaker. B's fully justified Arabic text produces wide word gaps (B1, B2), while A's ragged setting reads more evenly. B's dark header band on interior pages is a small plus, but A is cleaner overall.

A sets the Arabic in a lighter, more refined naskh-style face with generous line spacing, which makes for calmer and more readable text. B's heavier kufi-style face sits in a larger, denser text block that feels cramped. B's last page is better filled than A's sparse page 3. Even so, A's typographic quality and page rhythm read better overall.

B flows its text continuously and fits the relief photo onto the same page as the passage it illustrates (B5), so it avoids A's half-empty pages. A6 holds the image alone with a large blank area, and A5 ends early. A's dark header bands and boxed section heading (A3) are polished, but its section breaks are uneven: one heading is a heavy band and the other is plain text. B uses consistent rule-separated headings and tighter, more even pages.

B's bolder, numbered section headings stand out more clearly than A's thin heading-plus-rule treatment. Its sans Arabic body text also reads a little cleaner and more even. Both designs share the same cover-band structure and page flow, and both leave a large gap at the end of the last page.

A sets the Arabic text in a Naskh face with comfortable leading and adds running heads that name the current section, which helps navigation (A4, A5). B uses a geometric Kufi-style face that reads as heavier and more crowded. Its justification stretches lines unevenly (B3, B6), and it spills into a seventh page that holds only a few lines (B7). Both covers are comparable.

A sets the text more compactly across five pages, with clear running headers in a dark band that show section names. B adds a table of contents on B2, but it is sparse, its leader rows are faint, and its Latin numerals look mismatched. B also has wider spacing that stretches the text to seven pages, and the final page B7 is mostly empty. A's headings sit cleanly within the flow, as on A3 and A4.

A includes a table of contents (A2) and numbered, bolder section headings (A4, A5) that give clearer navigation, and its body text reads evenly. B adds a navy running-header band (B2–B5) but drops the TOC and numbering. Its headings are light and less distinct, and its fully justified Arabic lines show stretched gaps (B2).

B uses a larger, justified Arabic text block with consistent margins. Its running header band on B2–B3 and the navy title band tie the pages together, and the content fills pages more evenly. A's ragged, smaller text and the headings that run past the margin on A1 look less polished, and A3 is mostly empty. A's typeface is slightly more elegant, but B reads more comfortably overall.

A runs a consistent, larger body text with numbered, bold section headings, a table of contents, and running headers, so it reads evenly. B uses small, dense body paragraphs and switches to a larger size mid-page (B2, B3, B4). Its headings are light and unnumbered, so the hierarchy is weaker. Both show leftover broken image markup.

Both designs have the same cover and the same broken image-markdown text. A sets its section headings in strong dark bands (A3, A4), which give a clear visual signal. However, A's pages show uneven justification gaps and its subsection headings are inconsistent with the banded ones. B adds a contents page (B2) and numbered headings with running section headers (B3–B7), giving clearer navigation and steadier pacing. B's text flows continuously, though its last page is sparse (B7). On balance, B's navigational structure makes it the better document to read and keep.

A's Arabic body text is larger and more generously leaded, so it reads more comfortably. Its page fills are more even, and its subheading 'مقالة رئيسية' is better differentiated. B's text is smaller and denser, which crowds B2. B3 is also left largely empty, although B has a useful running header.

B gives each section heading a strong dark band (B3, B4) and adds running headers with page numbering "2 / 6", which makes the structure clear. A only uses thin rules and small headings. A's lead paragraphs use a larger font (A2, A4), but the size jumps unevenly. A also leaves a heading stranded near the bottom of a page (A2). B's text sits in a more uniform justified block. Both designs show raw broken image markdown. B's justified lines sometimes spread out widely at those spots (B4, B6). Even so, B reads as the more coherent and polished document.

Both designs share the same structure. A's justified Arabic text produces visibly stretched word spacing (A1, A2), and its long lines are harder to read. B's ragged lines read more evenly (B1, B2), and its numbered, bold headings make the sections clearer. B's lighter typeface is a bit plainer, though, and A's divider rules give a modest structural cue.

A sets the Arabic body in a calmer naskh-style face with comfortable leading. Its section heading 'العصر الفرعوني' falls at the bottom of A4, which is a minor orphan, but A5 then flows cleanly. B uses a geometric sans with tighter, darker text blocks that feel denser on B2–B5. B5 runs nearly a full page of text, while B2 leaves some uneven fill. B's heavy navy header bars also compete with the content. Both designs share the same image page and cover approach.

Design A has a table of contents (A2), numbered headings and running headers, and its body text runs continuously from page to page. Design B has a dramatic chapter divider (B3), but its sidebar band lists only two items. It has no TOC, its section 2 lacks a divider, and B5 is left mostly empty. B's display font also reads less cleanly at body size. A is more consistent and easier to navigate.

B packs the text more efficiently and sets the Hapi relief directly beneath the hymn introduction on B5, keeping image and context together. A runs the same content to six pages and leaves A5 ending on an introductory colon with the image isolated on A6 above a mostly empty page. A's narrower measure and running headers are tidy, and its numbered headings are clear. B's section rule and headings on B3 and B4 still read well, but B's denser pages give a steadier flow.

A runs its content compactly. Section headings sit in dark banded boxes, and running headers show section names. B spends a full page on a divider (B3) that lists only two sections and leaves much of the page empty. It also leaves B5 mostly blank, and it drops the section band in favour of a plain heading on B6. Both designs show the same raw image-markdown text. B's divider adds visual drama but breaks the reading flow and wastes space.

A sets the text in a comfortable size with even spacing, and its section breaks are simple rules. It integrates the relief image with its lead-in text on A5. B's dark heading band and running header give stronger structure. However, B's body text is dense and tightly justified, with visible stretched gaps (B2–B4). B's image is isolated on B6 with half a page empty below it, which separates the quoted lead-in on B5 from the figure.

A has a dramatic section divider (A3), but its body text is heavily justified with wide word gaps (A2, A4), and it misplaces the first section heading. The first section's text sits on A4 with no heading, and the second section opens with a rule but no number (A6). A also wastes most of A5 on a broken image link. B gives a proper table of contents (B2) and numbered section headings inline (B3, B5, B6). Its running headers name the current section, and its tighter, more even body text produces a coherent, navigable flow over fewer pages.

A uses a larger, clearer Arabic body face with comfortable line length and a restrained navy header, and its pages fill more evenly. B's smaller, lighter text runs in longer lines that are harder to read. B also leaves a large empty area on B1 and on most of B3, which makes its pacing uneven.

A sets the Arabic body larger, with comfortable leading and consistent margins, and its navy header band plus running heads read as polished. B's body text is small and light, which makes it harder to read. B also has a uneven blank area at the bottom of B1, the heading on B1 sits slightly misaligned against the right margin, and its bright blue band feels harsher.

Design A sets the Arabic text in a lighter face that renders unevenly, with ragged justification. Its section headings are small and faint, and pages A3 and A4 break awkwardly, leaving A5 mostly empty. Design B uses a cleaner, darker Arabic face with full justification and clearer section heads. A navy running-header band and page numbering ('2 / 5') help orientation, and the text flows continuously across B2–B5. B's text is dense, but it reads more consistently overall.

A uses a clearer Arabic text face with comfortable leading and a table of contents, with simple numbered headings. B adds strong navy section bands that give its headings punch, but its body text is denser with tighter justification, and the broken image-path text is spread awkwardly with large justified gaps (B6). On A the same broken path is more compact (A5, A7). A's sparse TOC page (A2) is a small cost.

B sets the text more compactly and finishes on six pages, where A needs seven and leaves A7 nearly empty with only a few lines. B's running headers carry the section names, which helps navigation (B4, B5). Its Naskh-style body type reads more naturally than A's rounded geometric face (A3–A6 vs B3–B6). A has slightly airier margins, but its pagination is weaker.

A sets the Arabic in a clear Naskh-style face with numbered, bold section headings and running headers, giving a cleaner hierarchy. B's geometric Arabic face with full justification creates uneven word gaps (B1, B2). Its headings are light and unnumbered, separated only by rules. The section that splits across B2–B3 also weakens rhythm, while A keeps section 2 intact on A2.

A uses one justified body face at a comfortable size with strong navy heading bands and running headers, so the pages read consistently. B switches body size and line spacing partway through. The lead paragraphs under each heading are large and loosely spaced, then the text drops to dense, small, tightly leaded blocks, which makes the rhythm feel uneven. B's thin rule headings also give weaker section cues. Both designs show the broken image markdown.

Both share the same layout, but B sets the Arabic body in a lighter, more even face with less ragged justification. A's wider letterspacing produces stretched gaps, visible in A1 and A2. B's bullets and running headers are cleaner. A's dark header bands add weight, but the differences overall are small.

The two designs share a near-identical structure. B marks the major section with a full-width green band and fills its pages with steadier text blocks (B3, B4). A uses small numbered headings, and A4 ends with a large empty area below the text. B's band gives clearer section hierarchy and a better reading rhythm. Typography is comparable in both.

A sets the Arabic in a larger naskh face with consistent headers and footers. Its section on the importance of tides fits on page 2, with no mid-paragraph break across pages. B uses a smaller, lighter face and splits a paragraph across B2–B3. B's subtitle 'مقالة رئيسية' is oversized and grey, competing with the heading. B's running header is also missing on B2–B3, so its layout feels less consistent.

B adds a table of contents, running headers with section names, and numbered section headings that stand out clearly. A's headings are small and weak, its text is dense and small, and it leaves a mostly empty final page. B's larger Arabic text with diacritics reads more comfortably, and its pages fill evenly.

A uses numbered section headings in bold, and its running headers carry section context, which gives a clearer hierarchy. Its Arabic face reads more cleanly with even justification. B's headings are unnumbered and weaker, and its justified text shows more stretched spacing. B also ends with a nearly empty final page.

B uses larger, more open body text with generous leading. Its divider page (B3) gives the sections clear structure, and its top rules are consistent across pages. A sets dense, small body text and places a section heading in the bottom quarter of A2, with the next paragraph continuing in a different size on A3. Its body size is inconsistent: it is lead-sized on A2 and A4 but small elsewhere. B has a weak half-empty page (B5) and a justified, gappy broken-image line, yet overall it reads more comfortably.

Both layouts share the same structure and banded cover. A sets the Arabic in a naskh-style face with ragged lines, which reads naturally and avoids gaps. B uses a geometric sans with full justification, producing visibly stretched word gaps and uneven texture, most noticeably in the bullet and paragraph blocks on B2 and B3. B's dark header strip is a minor plus, but A's text color is more comfortable to read.

A leaves page 5 half empty and puts the image alone on page 6 with a large blank area below it, so the flow breaks. B runs the text continuously and places the figure directly after the paragraph it belongs to, which gives a tighter rhythm. A's green section band is a nice touch, but its page breaks waste space.

Design B uses numbered section headings, running headers carrying the section name, and a smoother Arabic text face with even justification, which makes it easier to navigate and read. Design A's rule-separated headings are clean and its stylized font has some character. However, its heavy justification stretches the text in places (A1, A2), and its line spacing makes the text feel looser and less consistent. B's typesetting is tighter and more uniform (B2, B3).

B numbers its sections (1, 2, 3, 3.1) both in the table of contents and in the headings. This makes the structure clear at a glance. Its sans Arabic face is cleaner and slightly larger. A's section headings, such as بسكرة and فاس, are weak and barely distinguished from the body text. Otherwise the layouts are nearly identical.

B uses a cleaner Arabic typeface with tighter but even justification, avoiding A's stretched word gaps on A2–A4. A's full-width navy heading band on A3 gives a stronger section marker, and its dark header bars are distinctive. B's numbered headings and thin rules feel calmer, and its continuous flow (B3) avoids A's page break before 'التسمية' that leaves A3 dense. Both share the same weak half-empty image page, so the overall difference is modest.

A sets the Arabic text in a sans face with generous, justified line spacing. Its solid navy header bands give each page a clear running head. Major sections start on fresh pages; for example, A5 opens 'العصر الفرعوني' at the top of the page. B uses denser serif text with tighter leading and only thin rule headers. In B, the section 'العصر الفرعوني' begins near the bottom of B4, which reads crowded. Both designs place the image the same way, leaving the rest of the page empty.

Design A has a striking divider/TOC page (A3) with a large section title, but A5 ends half-empty and its first section has no in-text heading. Design B uses consistent dark heading bands (B3, B4), running headers that show the current section, and denser, more continuous pages without stranded gaps. B's flow is steadier and its navigation clearer. Both share the same broken image-markup text.

A uses a clean, quiet layout with thin running heads and plain numbered section headings, giving calm, readable body text. B's dark header bar on every page and heavy navy band behind the 'التسمية' heading feel heavy. Its justified text also shows wider word gaps, making the body text a little less even. B's banded heading adds emphasis, but A reads more comfortably overall.

The two designs are close. A's running header band carries section titles, and its sans byline matches the body text. B pairs a serif byline with the Arabic text, which reads as mismatched. A's pages keep consistent margins and a clear heading hierarchy. B uses a narrower measure, giving larger, more airy text but more rag. It also splits a paragraph across B2 and B3, while A keeps that paragraph whole on A2. A looks slightly more polished.

A uses larger, more open Arabic body text with generous leading, plus a header band with running titles that aids navigation. B's body text is smaller and denser, with weaker section headings and no header band. A's justified text is slightly stretched in places, but it is more comfortable to read overall.

A adds a table of contents (A2) that B lacks, which aids navigation, but its subsections break pages unevenly: an orphaned near-empty last page (A7) and short pages like A4/A6 leave ragged bottoms. B runs text continuously and fills its pages evenly (B2–B5). It also adds a navy header band with a running section title (B3, B4), which gives stronger page rhythm and wayfinding. Overall B reads as more cohesive and economical.

A provides a table of contents, running headers with section names, and a body font whose diacritics render cleanly. B's Arabic font shows broken glyph shapes (odd characters in words like خلدون) and B drops the running headers. A is more navigable and more legible, despite its sparse TOC page and short final page.

B provides a table of contents, running headers with rules, and a slightly larger, more open text setting with clearer heading separation, giving better navigation and a more finished document. A uses a denser, slightly stylised font that reads less comfortably, has no TOC or headers, and leaves a mostly empty final page. B's TOC page is sparse, but it is functional.

A sets its headings in a bold weight with section numbers, which gives a clear hierarchy. B uses light, unnumbered headings separated by rules, and they are less distinct. A's body text has more generous leading, making the Arabic easier to read. B's lines feel tighter, and its mixed Latin serif ('Lunar tide') clashes with the Arabic text. Layouts and page bands are otherwise near-identical.

A sets body text at a larger size with generous line spacing and a clear section divider page (A3), so it reads comfortably. B packs smaller text densely across full-width lines with tight leading (B2, B5) and mixes sizes awkwardly. A does have a mostly empty page (A5), but its overall readability is better.

A uses larger, more readable body text and bold numbered section headings that stand out clearly. B's headings are light, unnumbered and close to body size, separated only by thin rules, and its smaller body text with wide line spacing reads less comfortably. A's navy header band and running headers are more refined.

B uses a larger, cleaner Arabic sans with generous leading, numbered section headings, and running headers with rules, giving clearer hierarchy and easier reading. A's text is smaller and denser, though its figure sits with its lead-in text on A5 rather than alone on a mostly empty page as in B6.

A sets the Arabic text in a Naskh-style face with generous line spacing, which reads more comfortably than B's geometric sans with tighter, darker lines. A also includes a table of contents (A2) that aids navigation, though that page is mostly empty. B's navy header band is neat but heavier. Both covers are comparable.

A uses a larger, more open Arabic face with generous leading and a consistent top rule band on each page, and it adds a contents page. B sets a dense, small text block with tight leading that is harder to read. Its headings are weaker, it has no TOC, and the plain mid-blue cover is less refined.

B adds a table of contents (B2) that orients the reader. Its body text is set in a lighter, more refined Arabic face with comfortable margins and clearer section headings (B3–B5). A's dark header bands and larger, denser text (A2–A4) feel heavier. A's cover band is stronger, but B reads more comfortably overall.

A sets its text in a stylised Arabic display face with wide justification gaps. Its subheads are larger and more distinct (A1). B uses a calmer Naskh-style text face. Its running headers and footers help navigation (B2, B3). B also flows section 'كيفية حدوث' fully on B2 without an awkward mid-sentence split, while A splits it across A2 and A3. B's body text reads more evenly. A's title band and subhead contrast are slightly stronger.

B has numbered headings and a numbered TOC, running headers showing the current section, and a tighter page flow that ends with only a modest trailing gap on B6. A's last page, A7, is a near-empty orphan with three lines. A's display font has a narrower, more stylized look and its headings are less distinct (A6, A4). B's text block reads more evenly (B3–B5).
